'''''Rebutia minuscula''''' is a species of [[cactus]] from South America found in northern [[Argentina]] and [[Bolivia]].<ref name="Ande01p605">{{Citation |last=Anderson |first=Edward'' f. ''|year=2001 |title=The Cactus Family |publication-place=Pentland, Oregon |publisher=Timber Press |isbn=978-0-88192-498-5 }}, p. 605</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Fearn |first=Brian |title=The Genus Rebutia |publisher=Abbey Brook Cactus Nursery |year=1981 |pages=4}}</ref> It is the [[type (biology)|type species]] of the genus ''[[Rebutia]]''.{{sfn|ps=|Anderson|2001|p=599}} As its synonym ''Rebutia senilis'' it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = "AGM2020" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=December 2020 |page=91 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=19 May 2021 }}</ref> Its cultivars 'Krainziana', 'Marsoneri' and 'Violaciflora' are also listed as having gained the Award of Garden Merit.<ref name = "AGM2020" />

The status of the species of ''Rebutia'' is currently uncertain; indeed the genus as defined by Anderson (2001) has been shown to be [[Polyphyly|polyphyletic]].<ref name=RitzMartMeckGore07>{{Citation |last=Ritz |first=Christiane M. |last2=Martins |first2=Ludwig |last3=Mecklenburg |first3=Rainer |last4=Goremykin |first4=Vadim |last5=Hellwig |first5=Frank H. |year=2007 |title=The molecular phylogeny of ''Rebutia'' (Cactaceae) and its allies demonstrates the influence of paleogeography on the evolution of South American mountain cacti |journal=American Journal of Botany |volume=94 |pages=1321–1332 |name-list-style=amp |doi=10.3732/ajb.94.8.1321 |pmid=21636499|doi-access= }}</ref> Anderson describes ''R. minuscula'' as consisting of globe-shaped stems with a diameter of up to {{convert|5|cm|in|abbr=on|0}}, forming large clusters. The stem has 16–20 ribs with small but distinct tubercles ("bumps"). Each [[areole]] produces 25–30 fine whitish spines, {{convert|1|-|3|mm|in|abbr=on|1}} long. As in other species of ''Rebutia'', the flowers are not produced at the top of the stem, but from around the base. They are red, up to {{convert|4|cm|in|abbr=on|1}} long.<ref name=Ande01p605/> Other authorities include synonyms such as ''R.{{nbsp}}marsoneri'', with yellow to orange flowers, in ''R. minuscula'', giving the species a much broader range of flower colour.{{sfn|ps=|Anderson|2001|p=604}}<ref name=Shea12>{{Citation |last=Sheader |first=Martin |year=2012 |title=Show Reports: Summer Show South |journal=The Alpine Gardener |volume=80 |issue=1 |pages=88–91 }}</ref>
